high.title: Investors React to Vale (VALE3), Santander (SANB11) Earnings and Selic Cut; Ibovespa in Dollar Terms Rises Today (29)
high.summary: Super Wednesday arrives with dual monetary policy decisions from Brazil's COPOM and the US Federal Reserve, both pressured by Middle East conflict and rising oil prices. Brazilian markets expect a 0.25pp Selic cut from 14.75% to 14.50%, continuing the monetary easing cycle initiated in the last meeting. The US FOMC is expected to hold rates between 3.50%-3.75%. The meeting gains additional significance as it may be Jerome Powell's final session before his mandate expires May 15th. Investors are also digesting earnings results, with Vale (VALE3) reporting Q1 net profit of US$1.9 billion, up 36% year-over-year. The dual rate decisions are critical for BRL positioning and capital flows, as Brazil's easing cycle contrasts with US policy pause. Markets will watch for COPOM's forward guidance and any signals about the pace of future cuts, which could significantly impact Brazilian bonds and currency dynamics.

high.title: Former Central Bank Official Diogo Guillen Takes Position as Chief Economist at Itaú Unibanco
high.summary: Itaú Unibanco announced a significant change in its Economic Research leadership. Starting July 1st, Diogo Guillen will assume the role of chief economist after completing his quarantine period. Guillen brings recent experience from Brazil's Central Bank, where he served as Economic Policy Director from 2022-2025, and previously worked in Itaú's asset management economic area from 2015-2021. He holds a PhD from Princeton University. Guillen replaces Mário Mesquita, who leaves at the end of April after nearly a decade leading Macroeconomics and Research since July 2016. This transition is significant for markets as the chief economist role at Brazil's largest private bank carries substantial influence over market expectations and monetary policy interpretation. Guillen's Central Bank background provides valuable insight into BCB thinking, which could enhance Itaú's research credibility during a crucial period of monetary policy transition.

high.title: Central Bank (BC) Decrees Extrajudicial Liquidation of Currency Broker for 'Serious Irregularities'
high.summary: The Central Bank of Brazil decreed the extrajudicial liquidation of Frente Corretora de Câmbio S.A., a São Paulo-based currency broker, due to compromised financial situation and serious violations of legal and regulatory norms. The institution is classified in the "S4" segment of prudential regulation and has low relevance in the National Financial System. In the BC's currency ranking, the broker occupied 78th position, representing only 0.021% of financial volume and 0.054% of transactions in the SFN during 2025. While this specific case has minimal systemic impact, it demonstrates the Central Bank's continued vigilance over FX market participants during a period of currency volatility and reflects ongoing regulatory enforcement in Brazil's foreign exchange sector.

medium.title: Banco do Brasil (BBAS3) Diagnosis for Agribusiness: 'If Selic Falls, the Sector Reacts Quickly'
medium.summary: Banco do Brasil's VP of Agribusiness believes the sector will respond quickly to continued Selic rate cuts. With a R$406 billion agribusiness portfolio, the bank expects stability in 2026. The executive noted that part of delinquency is concentrated in large machinery and input industries, and lower interest rates would favor new investments and financial problem solutions. BB projects R$3 billion in business at Agrishow fair.

medium.title: Braskem (BRKM5) Receives Indications from Novonor and Petrobras (PETR4) for Board, Including Magda Chambriard
medium.summary: Braskem received new board nominations from shareholders Novonor and Petrobras for the Ordinary General Meeting. Notable appointments include Magda Chambriard, current Petrobras president, as board chairman, and Héctor Nuñez, Novonor's CEO, as vice-chairman. This comes after Novonor signed a contract to sell control to Shine I FIP fund, representing approximately 50.1% of ordinary shares and 34.3% of total capital.

medium.title: Bank of England Maintains Interest Rates and Assesses Iran War Risks for Inflation
medium.summary: The Bank of England held rates at 3.75% with an 8-1 vote, with only chief economist Huw Pill seeking a 4.0% increase. The committee is monitoring Middle East developments closely and defined scenarios for Iran war's economic impact, including potential "vigorous" rate increases. This follows Fed and precedes ECB decisions, highlighting global central bank coordination during geopolitical tensions that could affect commodity prices and inflation expectations.

medium.title: Nubank (ROXO34) and Mercado Livre (MELI34) Enter List of Most Influential Financial Sector Companies
medium.summary: Nubank and Mercado Livre were included in TIME's first TIME100 Companies: Industry Leaders ranking for most influential financial sector companies in 2026. Their inclusion reflects the advancement of digital models in financial services beyond traditional banks, particularly in a region historically marked by low banking inclusion. Mercado Pago has 78 million monthly active users and generated $12.6 billion net revenue in 2025.
